title: Flatness and structure-sheaf cohomology of canonical projective-bundle fibres
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal E$ a quasi-coherent finite locally free $\mathcal O_S$-module of constant positive rank $r$ [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module], and $p:\mathbf P(\mathcal E)\to S$ its canonical symmetric-algebra relative Proj [def-trf-canonical-symmetric-graded-algebra]. Then $p$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. For every $s\in S$, the residue-field fibre $\mathbf P(\mathcal E)_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is geometrically reduced and geometrically connected [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], and $H^1(\mathbf P(\mathcal E)_s,\mathcal O)=0$, with cohomology of the underlying abelian structure sheaf [def-sc-structure-sheaf-cohomology-pullback].

proof.text: Choose local frames for E. Open compatibility of canonical symmetric relative Proj and the free comparison in projective_bundle_quotient_geometry identify the projection over every frame open with standard projective (r-1)-space. On homogeneous standard opens the projection is the polynomial projection. The polynomial ring in finitely many variables is flat and finitely presented over the base, and these properties are local on source and target. Thus p is flat and locally of finite presentation.

Base change a frame at s to Spec kappa(s). The quotient description identifies the fibre over kappa(s) with projective (r-1)-space, compatibly with all field extensions. Over any field extension its standard charts are polynomial rings, hence reduced and integral, and their pairwise overlaps are nonempty. The chart cover gives reducedness and connectedness. This establishes both geometric properties.

For r>=2 apply the projective-space twist-cohomology computation to O(0). Its positive cohomology vanishes, including H1. For r=1 the fibre is the affine spectrum of its residue field and affine acyclicity gives H1=0. Identify the structure sheaf under the fibre isomorphism; forget the module action to get the displayed abelian-sheaf cohomology vanishing. There is no s on an empty base.

lean.statement:
theorem projective_bundle_fiber_geometry (S : Scheme.{u}) (E : S.Modules)
    [E.IsQuasicoherent] (r : ℕ)
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E r] (hr : 0 < r) :
    let p := (SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjHom
    Flat p ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation p ∧
      ∀ s : S, GeometricallyReduced (p.fiberToSpecResidueField s) ∧
        GeometricallyConnected (p.fiberToSpecResidueField s) ∧
        Subsingleton (Sheaf.H (Scheme.structureSheafAb (p.fiber s)) 1)
